title: AI’s Regimes of Representation: A Community-centered Study of Text-to-Image Models in South Asia
benchmark_measurement: The study measured how text-to-image models perpetuate stereotypical, one-dimensional, and homogenizing representations of religious groups and practices within the South Asian cultural context. This included the erasure of religious diversity (e.g., 'Hinduization' of Indian iconography), the reduction of Muslim life to narrow religious symbols (mosques, veils), and the default to Western religious norms (Christian churches) for generic prompts.
findings: The study found that text-to-image models perpetuate harmful religious tropes and erase diversity. For generic prompts like 'a house of worship,' models defaulted to generating Christian churches. Within the Indian context, there was a significant 'Hinduization of Indian religious iconography,' which erased the nation's minority religions like Islam, Christianity, and Buddhism. Furthermore, representations of Muslim lives were found to be one-dimensional and stereotypical, frequently reduced to religious iconography such as mosques, prayer caps, and veils for all individuals, which participants linked to reductive Western media narratives.
references: Murphie A. and Potts J. 2017. Culture and technology. Bloomsbury Publishing.
